title: Ghost Walk take visitors on unexplained journey
excerpt: There are stories of Lawrenceburg found in history books and old newspaper archives—and then there are stories born from first-hand experiences, that leave room for questions and interpretation.
content:
There are stories of Lawrenceburg found in history books and old newspaper archives—and then there are stories born from first-hand experiences, that leave room for questions and interpretation.

During the Lawrenceburg Ghost Walk, tour guide and paranormal investigator Jeff Waldridge explores both—taking visitors to some of the city’s historic buildings while sharing documented history and stories from his own paranormal investigations at these locations.

During the recent Burgoo Festival, Waldridge hosted after-dark ghost tours on both Friday and Saturday nights, drawing festival-goers interested in the unusual and paranormal history of Anderson County.

His tour began on Main Street with a walk to the Anderson County Courthouse. Under the dark October sky, with purple candles lit in the courthouse windows, Waldridge began his unique history lesson.

He recounted the history of the courthouse rebuildings, the Lawrenceburg fires, the old jailhouse, and several people who died in the building over the years. He then showed photos of the courthouse at different time periods before sharing his personal experiences—of getting permission to investigate the courthouse and his multiple investigations alongside local officials and law enforcement.

Throughout the tour, Waldridge played several audio recordings and EVPs which included voices, an old-fashioned telephone ringing, and even a “ghost cough” which Waldridge found amusing. He also showed a photo of a man’s shadow on the courthouse roof and explained that a number of people have reported seeing a man’s silhouette in the same spot many times.

Later in the tour, the group stood outside a building on Main Street looking at the upstairs portion where an old hotel connected to the former Lawrenceburg opera house was once located.

This portion of the building currently has no electricity, and Waldridge shared that the owners have kept it closed due to their concerns about paranormal activity. In this building, Waldridge has even sat for hours in the dark just to see what really happens, and he shared several recordings and photos from his experiences at this location with the tour group.

“I started doing research and everything in 2012, and I’ve been a paranormal investigator for close to 30 years,” said Waldridge. “So it’s all done from that point of view.”

“One thing that I was very particular about was the history, and then I personally investigated every location that’s on the tour.”

Waldridge is both a lifelong resident of Lawrenceburg and a lifelong investigator of the paranormal. In 2014, he combined his interests with his hometown and started the Lawrenceburg Ghost Walk.

Since then, he has continued to research the history and unusual activities of Lawrenceburg, and he even wrote a book titled The Haunting of a Bourbon Town.

This year, Waldridge will host two more ghost walks on Oct. 30-31 before closing up for the season. Both walks will be at 8 p.m. starting at Century Bank Park. Tickets are $15 and can be purchased at kyghosttours.com.

When he’s not hosting ghost walks, Waldridge can be found doing paranormal events across the nation with his company, Creepy People Management, such as an event called Cryptagon which is a Big Foot, Monsters, and Legends convention.

No matter what he is doing, Waldridge believes in doing the research personally.

“I’ve investigated these buildings for hours and hours on end, and I’ve got some amazing evidence—recordings, video, pictures that I show,” he said. “You’re getting more than just walking around, and I can 100% guarantee that the history is authentic.”

For Waldridge, that research is what separates the stories from simple ghost stories—giving visitors a chance to experience a different side of Lawrenceburg’s history and decide for themselves what they believe.
